usuario.title: Hearing Aid User
usuario.description: Tips to improve your daily communication.
usuario.subtitle: Choose a topic below.

ambientes.title: Communication Environments
ambientes.paragraph1: There are environments that create echoes, such as kitchens, bathrooms, tiled rooms, and churches, which make understanding more difficult. Places with many people, a lot of noise, or even low lighting can make it harder to focus and understand what is being said, affecting comprehension and conversation.
ambientes.paragraph2: Whenever possible, try to talk in well-lit and quiet environments. If that is not possible, try to stay focused on what is being said and always ask when you do not fully understand.

desconforto.title: What if there is discomfort?
desconforto.description: What to do when the hearing aid causes discomfort?
desconforto.paragraph1: In the first few days of use, there may be situations in which you need to remove the device or start by using it for a shorter time during the day to gradually get used to it and to the new sounds more easily. Wearing a hearing aid is like wearing glasses.
desconforto.paragraph2: The difficulty exists and adaptation can be challenging. But with continued use, it gets better and the day can be enjoyed more fully.

duvidas.title: I Still Have Questions
duvidas.description: If you still have questions about communication, contact your speech-language pathologist.
duvidas.paragraph1: Always seek your speech-language pathologist if you have questions or problems. Whenever doubts or issues arise with the hearing aid or during the elderly person’s adaptation process, contact the professional so they can help.

entender.title: I Couldn't Understand, Now What?
entender.description: What to do when you cannot understand what is being said?
entender.paragraph1: Attention is extremely important in the communication process. If we are talking to someone but thinking about what we need to do later—go to the market, clean the house—we will not be able to understand.
entender.paragraph2: Not because we did not hear, but because our attention was elsewhere. And if I paid attention but still did not understand? It is important to ask the person to repeat the information you did not understand, because they may not always realize whether you understood or not.
entender.paragraph3: You can ask questions or give clues that show you did not understand. For example: “I didn’t understand, please speak more slowly.” Or “Could you please repeat that a little louder?” or “Sorry, what? Please speak while looking at me!”

uso.title: Hearing Aid Use
uso.description: The importance of using the hearing aid.
uso.paragraph1: It is necessary to use the hearing aid for as long as possible each day. However, in the first few days of use, there may be situations in which he or she needs to remove the device or start using it for a shorter time during the day to gradually get used to it and to the new sounds more easily.
uso.paragraph2: Wearing a hearing aid is like wearing glasses: the difficulty exists and adaptation can be challenging. But with use, it gets better and the day can be enjoyed more fully!
uso.paragraph3: That is why it is essential that people who live with elderly individuals encourage and remind them to use the hearing aid and create situations that make listening and understanding easier.

possiveis-problemas.title: Possible Problems
possiveis-problemas.description: Learn about possible issues that may occur with the hearing aid.
possiveis-problemas.paragraph1: It is important to stay alert to some situations that may indicate it is time to schedule a follow-up appointment with the speech-language pathologist: if the elderly person feels discomfort with the fit or earmold of the hearing aid;
possiveis-problemas.paragraph2: Or mentions that a part is crooked or very dirty inside; in addition, the elderly person may notice that the hearing aid is producing a whistling sound even when nothing is nearby.
possiveis-problemas.paragraph3: Do not hesitate to suggest or even take the elderly person to the speech-language pathologist responsible for their fitting. Hearing aids are delicate and must be well cared for to improve the quality of life of those who matter to us.

como-comunicar.title: How to communicate
como-comunicar.paragraph1: Communication is a two-way process. It is necessary to connect with the person you are speaking to and give them space to speak as well. Therefore, when communicating, it is important to look directly at the face of the person you are talking to.
como-comunicar.paragraph2: When you speak while looking at the person, you provide more cues to help them understand what you are saying and feeling. This is especially important when communicating with people with hearing loss, who often rely on lip reading. Imagine watching a movie in a language you are not fluent in—it becomes much easier with subtitles. The same happens with a person with hearing loss, but your face becomes the subtitle of their communication.

outros-cuidados-aasi.title: Other Precautions
outros-cuidados-aasi.description: Learn about other necessary care for the hearing aid.
outros-cuidados-aasi.paragraph1: It is important to remember that hearing aids are sensitive to high temperatures. Therefore, when using a hair dryer or going to a beauty salon, remind the elderly person to remove the hearing aid.
outros-cuidados-aasi.paragraph2: Just as high temperatures are harmful, moisture and rain can also be damaging. Help the elderly person remember to protect the hearing aid in these situations.

parceiro.title: Communication Partner
parceiro.description: Tips for family members and friends.
parceiro.subtitle: Choose a topic below.

atencao.title: Ensure Attention and Understanding
atencao.paragraph1: Always communicate in a calm and peaceful manner. Always encourage him or her to participate in the conversation. This way, you ensure that the elderly person is included in the conversation, understands what is happening, and can share their opinions whenever they wish.
atencao.paragraph2: This supports not only hearing, but also cognition and the sense of belonging.

e-se-houver-desconforto.paragraph1: It's important to use the hearing aid for as long as possible, but initially you can start by using it for shorter periods during the day to get used to the device and new sounds more easily.
e-se-houver-desconforto.paragraph2: During the initial period of use, there may be situations where the elderly person needs to remove the device or start using it for shorter periods during the day to get used to the device and new sounds more easily. Using a hearing aid is like using glasses: there are difficulties and adaptation is challenging. But with use, it gets better, allowing for a more enjoyable day!

parceiros.title: Importance of Communication Partners
parceiros.description: It is important to understand the role of communication partners.
parceiros.paragraph1: Communication partners, that is, people who live and talk to the elderly, are fundamental in the day-to-day life and in the rehabilitation process. They are often the ones who notice hearing difficulties, seek medical and speech therapy. And they are the people who live with the elderly and talk to them. And most of the time they help in the use and handling of the device.
parceiros.paragraph2: Therefore, in order for there to be effective use and improvement in communication, In addition to the elderly person using the device, it is necessary for the communicative partner to use strategies that facilitate communication.

incentivo.title: Encouraging Hearing Aid Use
incentivo.description: Learn how to encourage the use of the hearing aid.
incentivo.paragraph1: The adaptation process is not easy. Elderly individuals may often forget to put on their hearing aids or believe they do not need them. That is why patience is necessary. Here is a tip: place reminders around the house.

estrategias-interlocutor.title: How to communicate
estrategias-interlocutor.description: Learn how to help the elderly person use the hearing aid.
estrategias-interlocutor.paragraph1: To make it easier to understand what is being said, we have some strategies. They are: Not screaming, Shouting or raising the voice distorts the sounds of speech, impairing the understanding of the hearing impaired. Do not exaggerate or reduce mouth movements when speaking, this impairs 'lip reading'. Always try to speak slower than normal, with an adequate voice and volumes.
estrategias-interlocutor.paragraph2: Avoid covering your face with gestures, sunglasses, a full beard, talking while eating or smoking. Especially in poorly lit areas, as this can also impair lip-reading. Speak as close to the person as possible as you can, the farther away, the more difficult the conversation. Explain better when you notice that the user of hearing aids they don't understand, using shorter sentences and/or replacing more complicated words with simpler words.

processo-adaptacao.title: Adaptation Process
processo-adaptacao.description: Understand the adaptation process to the hearing aid.
processo-adaptacao.paragraph1: The process of fitting hearing aids is a long one. It can take time for the patient to get used to new habits related to fitting and to get used to the presence of the hearing aids in their ears. You have to adapt to the weight and fit of the devices, as well as the hygiene routine. New connections will be re-established in the brain, just like downloading a file onto a computer.
processo-adaptacao.paragraph2: The more motivated the patient, the faster the hearing aid will become a part of them. Point out improvements, offer help, encourage use!

tempo-de-uso.title: Hearing Aid Use
tempo-de-uso.description: Learn the recommended daily hearing aid use for the hearing aid.
tempo-de-uso.paragraph1: Hearing aid use. It is important to encourage the use of hearing aids for as long as possible each day. Being able to communicate with the world promotes self-esteem and stimulates brain activity.
tempo-de-uso.paragraph2: Therefore, encourage the elderly person to wear their hearing aids for as long as possible throughout the day.
